paper.title: ARC: Warp-level Adaptive Atomic Reduction in GPUs to Accelerate Differentiable Rendering

reading.scope: Physical pages 2–13: differentiable-rendering workload, atomic reduction, hardware/software designs, evaluation and scope limits. Page 1 retains prior complete abstract reading; pages 14–20 are not declared read.

findings: High L2 hit rate does not eliminate atomic-request serialization or LSU queue pressure. Reducing traffic requires checking the actual contended resource.
Warp-local grouping trades fewer atomic requests for instruction, register and control-flow work; lane activity and address locality affect the break-even point.
ARC-HW changes an instruction and reduction hardware under simulation; ARC-SW uses shader-level alternatives measured on real GPUs. These are separate realizations.
The software threshold is workload-tuned periodically. The all-lane butterfly condition does not cover every rendering case or arbitrary irregular graph updates.
Commutativity, unused return values, atomicity assumptions and floating-point reduction order bound applicability. The paper does not prove bitwise equality or universal ML/RL suitability.
Kernel-level gradient results, whole training and simulated hardware parameters must not be merged into one speedup or a real-chip specification table.
paper_to_framework_gap: The paper links an ARC-SW artifact, but its code and current framework/CCCL integration were not read in this phase. Historical software-baseline limitations are not current-library support claims.
scope: Declared paper sections and visual pages only. Existing chapter resource/quality reasoning is sufficient; no new main section, case, lab or figure, no hardware or downloaded-code execution.
